body.statement: Derive a necessary-and-sufficient inequality in \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d\), including its boundary logarithms, for \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\). On its complement, characterize the order of \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\) from the matched deterministic optimizations delivered by oeq:complete-frontier, and exhibit legal sequences in the unchanged class that certify strict divergence.
body.justification: The value of knowing assignment is a derived experiment-comparison frontier, not a generic first-order product-rate slogan.
body.gap: The unchanged-class comparison now proves equality on the sufficient region \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\), and strict polynomial divergence on the sufficient region \(\gamma>\alpha+\beta\), \(d>2(\alpha+\beta)\gamma/(\gamma-\alpha-\beta)\).  A necessary-and-sufficient partition, the remaining ratio orders, and unresolved boundary logarithms are still open.
body.consumer: Study designers can determine when recording or externally supplying assignment probabilities changes the detectable scale of effect variation.

obligation.what_is_open: A necessary-and-sufficient equality region, the order of the radius ratio throughout the complementary regimes, and all unresolved boundary logarithms.
obligation.obstruction: The sparse converse and known-propensity benchmark now prove strict polynomial divergence in one explicit region, but the observational lower and upper maps remain unmatched outside the proved no-penalty region. Therefore they do not determine necessity, the exact threshold boundary, or the remaining complementary regimes.
obligation.attempted: Combined the same-class sparse nuisance lower bound with the known-propensity upper bound, verified that the strict dimension condition implies the sparse-regime hypothesis, and optimized the resulting exponent algebraically. Per the final-maximality directive, no new upper architecture was attempted.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  Two sufficient regions are proved on the unchanged class.  First,
\[
 s_0\ge\gamma\quad\text{and}\quad d\le4\gamma
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}.
\]
At \(d=4\gamma\), this comparison gives \(n^{-1/4}\) without a logarithm.  Second, if
\[
 \gamma>s_0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 d>\frac{2s_0\gamma}{\gamma-s_0},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \ge c n^{\frac{2\gamma}{4\gamma+d}-\frac{2s_0}{2s_0+d}}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The necessary-and-sufficient equality region is not yet established.  In particular, the regimes \(s_0\ge\gamma\) with \(d>4\gamma\), and \(\gamma>s_0\) with \(d\le 2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\), including the equality boundary and any transition logarithms there, remain unresolved.
